project.title: Placement Portal Application V2 Planner
project.subtitle: Flask + Vue execution dashboard
project.goal: Build all core requirements of the Placement Portal Application V2 using Flask, Vue SFCs, Bootstrap, SQLite, Redis, and Celery within a strict 2-3 week schedule while keeping the implementation viva-safe and locally demoable.
constraints: Use Flask for API, Vue 3 SFCs for UI, Bootstrap for styling, SQLite for DB, Redis for cache and Celery broker.
Implement only core requirements before any optional features.
Keep the UI minimal and reproducible with Bootstrap components.
Prioritize local demo reliability over architectural cleverness.
success_criteria: Admin, company, and student flows all work end-to-end.
Admin can approve companies and placement drives.
Students can apply only once and only when eligible.
CSV export, reminders, monthly reports, and Redis caching are demoable locally.

weeks.label: Week 1
weeks.goal: Remove setup risk and get the backend/frontend shells talking cleanly.
outputs: Repo scaffold with Flask backend and Vue frontend.

weeks.label: Week 2
weeks.goal: Complete the main admin, company, and student workflows.
outputs: Admin dashboard, approvals, search, and deactivation.
Company drive creation and application review flows.
Student dashboard, drive browsing, and apply flow.

weeks.label: Week 3
weeks.focus: Async jobs, cache, and viva prep
weeks.goal: Finish the operational requirements and harden the demo path.
outputs: CSV export via Celery and Redis.
Reminder and monthly HTML report jobs.
QA checklist, report assets, and demo rehearsal.

risks.title: Vue learning curve
risks.impact: Can slow the first week and delay auth wiring.
risks.mitigation: Learn Router, Pinia, forms, and API calls only; skip advanced Vue patterns.

risks.title: Auth integration drift
risks.impact: Frontend can stall if Flask-Security and SPA requests are not aligned early.
risks.mitigation: Finish login, me, logout, and route guards before admin/company/student dashboard work.

risks.title: Celery and Redis late failure
risks.impact: Async jobs can consume too much end-stage time.
risks.mitigation: Keep exports and report HTML minimal, prove one clean end-to-end task first, then extend.

risks.title: Scope creep
risks.impact: Optional features can break the core completion target.
risks.mitigation: Do not start charts, ATS, PWA, or fancy UI until all core flows are stable.

architecture.title: Backend
architecture.summary: Flask API with app factory and SQLAlchemy models.
points: Use blueprints grouped by auth, admin, company, student, and public.
Use programmatic DB creation and one seeded admin account.
Keep responses JSON-only for the Vue SPA.

architecture.title: Frontend
architecture.summary: Vue 3 with Vite, Router, Pinia, and Bootstrap.
points: Use SFC pages for auth and role dashboards.
Keep state management limited to auth and small shared UI state.
Build forms and tables with straightforward Bootstrap patterns.

architecture.title: Auth Model
architecture.summary: Unified User model with role separation and session-backed SPA auth.
points: Student and company self-register.
Admin is seeded only, with no registration UI.
Role guards protect both API routes and frontend navigation.

architecture.title: Async and Cache
architecture.summary: Redis powers both Celery and caching.
points: CSV export runs through a user-triggered async task.
Daily reminders and monthly reports run through scheduled jobs.
Cache read-heavy list and stats endpoints with explicit invalidation.

architecture.title: Storage
architecture.summary: Local-first storage keeps the demo simple.
points: SQLite file for relational data.
Local uploads folder for resumes.
Local report and export folders for generated files.

architecture.title: Guardrails
architecture.summary: The core demo path is more important than polish.
points: No optional features until the core checklist passes.
No complex calendar or notification system.
No styling work that blocks backend milestone progress.

models.name: Role
models.purpose: Defines admin, company, and student access groups.

models.name: User
models.purpose: Unified authentication record for all three roles.
models.relations: One-to-one with StudentProfile or CompanyProfile; many-to-many with Role.

models.name: StudentProfile
models.purpose: Stores student academic and placement-facing data.
models.relations: Belongs to User; one-to-many with Application and PlacementRecord.

models.name: CompanyProfile
models.purpose: Stores company registration and approval details.
models.relations: Belongs to User; one-to-many with PlacementDrive and PlacementRecord.

models.name: PlacementDrive
models.purpose: Represents a company recruitment event or job opening.
models.relations: Belongs to CompanyProfile; one-to-many with Application.

models.name: Application
models.purpose: Tracks a student's application to a placement drive.
models.relations: Belongs to StudentProfile and PlacementDrive; one-to-one optional with PlacementRecord.

models.name: PlacementRecord
models.relations: Linked to Application, StudentProfile, CompanyProfile, and PlacementDrive.

points: Admin is seeded and can log in.
Student and company can self-register.

acceptance_checks.title: Approval chain
points: Company stays blocked until admin approval.
Drive stays hidden from students until admin approval.
Blacklisting cuts off new actions without erasing history.

acceptance_checks.title: Student application flow
points: Only eligible students can apply.
Duplicate application to the same drive is blocked.
Student sees live status in application history.

acceptance_checks.title: Company review flow
points: Company can review only its own applicants.
Company can shortlist, reject, schedule interview, and select.
Selected state creates or updates placement history.

acceptance_checks.title: Async and cache
points: CSV export runs through Celery and Redis.
Daily reminder and monthly report jobs are runnable locally.

acceptance_checks.title: Submission readiness
